Where else to get help

The other places a small business or household can get technology help, who each one suits, and when they'd serve you better than neon1.

Type
Comparison
Edition
1.0
Updated
November 9, 2026
Facts checked
November 9, 2026
Download PDF

neon1 isn't the right fit for everyone. These are the main alternatives, how they usually charge, and when each would serve you better. Prices change, so check each provider's site.

OptionBest forUsually chargesBetter than neon1 when
Doing it yourself, with vendor supportOne task inside a tool you already useIncluded in your subscriptionThe product's own features and help cover it
Free advising: SCORE, NY Small Business Development Centers, public librariesPlanning and an independent second opinionFreeYou're still deciding what to do, or need business advice beyond technology
Freelance marketplaces: Upwork, FiverrA narrow, well-defined buildThe freelancer's price plus platform fees: Upwork adds 5% (Basic) or 10% (Business Plus) and a contract fee. Fiverr adds a fee at checkoutYou can write the specification and check the result yourself
Managed service providers (MSPs)Help desk, devices, and security for a teamA monthly fee per user or deviceYour staff need a help desk or someone to answer at 2 a.m.
Retail and repair shops, such as Best Buy's Geek SquadA broken device or a home installA price per job, or a membership that adds 24/7 supportA device needs parts, a repair, or a walk-in visit
AgenciesLarger builds that need a teamProject fees or retainersThe work needs several people at once, for months
Fractional CTO or IT directorTechnology leadership for a growing companyA monthly retainerYou need a leader in your meetings every week
Large consultanciesEnterprise programsLarge contractsYou need scale, formal methods, or audit services
Security specialists: MSSPs, auditors, penetration testersMonitoring, audits, formal testingRetainers or fixed engagementsYou need an audit opinion, a penetration test report, or 24/7 monitoring

Things to watch for

  • Freelancers: quality varies, and handover and documentation depend on who you pick. Make sure accounts are created in your name.
  • MSPs: long contracts, tools and accounts held in the provider's name, and exit fees. Ask how you'd leave before you sign. Provider-written 2026 pricing guides mostly put small-business plans around $100 to $250 per user per month.
  • Repair shops: they fix the device in front of them, but rarely look at how your tools work together.

Where neon1 fits

Owner-run businesses, small practices, and households that want their tools to work together, and want to understand and own the result, with documentation at handover. neon1 works by appointment and takes at most two clients at a time. It isn't the right choice for 24/7 coverage, a large team, formal assurance, or regulated professional judgment.

If you're not sure, ask. If I'm not the right person, I'll try to point you to someone who is.

Sources

Every provider's terms above were read on its own page on November 9, 2026. The managed IT range comes from pricing guides written by providers, so treat it as rough.
